title: Integrating ChatGPT in Grade 12 Quantum Theory Education: An Exploratory Study at Emirate School (UAE)
venue: International Journal of Information and Education Technology
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether integrating ChatGPT into Grade 12 Quantum Theory instruction improves student learning outcomes compared with traditional teaching. The stated problem is that although AI chatbots are receiving attention in education, their pedagogical value in Quantum Theory and STEM instruction remains underexplored. The study asks how technology integration affects students’ understanding of core concepts and how chatbot-supported practical learning experiences influence outcomes.

The intervention consisted of ChatGPT-enhanced instruction and customized chatbot-supported activities for Quantum Theory, delivered to an experimental group, while a control group received traditional instruction. The study used a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test comparison alongside qualitative interviews, making it a mixed-methods study. Quantitative outcomes were measured with a 30-item Quantum Theory achievement test covering Knowing, Applying, and Reasoning. Qualitative data came from semi-structured interviews about students’ experiences using ChatGPT.

Participants were 112 18-year-old third-semester students from schools in the Al Ain zone in the United Arab Emirates, including an experimental group of 55 and a control group of 57. The context appears to be school-based, in-person Quantum Theory education at the Grade 12 level. Students in the experimental condition used ChatGPT to ask questions, receive explanations, support problem solving, and engage in collaborative discussions around course content.

The main conclusion is that ChatGPT-enhanced instruction was associated with significantly higher post-test scores than traditional teaching, including improvements in Knowing, Applying, and Reasoning, with reported large effect sizes. Qualitative findings suggested greater engagement, better comprehension, improved problem-solving, and stronger perceived relevance of the subject. At the same time, students reported limitations such as insufficient depth for some complex topics, inability to interpret graphs well, and occasional mathematical errors. The authors conclude that ChatGPT has promise as a supplementary instructional tool, while emphasizing the need for further research on long-term effects and broader educational contexts.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental mixed-methods K-12 study with a comparison group and pre/post testing, which supports moderate causal inference. However, it is not randomized, uses a researcher-developed test, and reporting is inconsistent in places, so it falls below blue-tier rigor.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports large positive achievement effects for the ChatGPT condition, with eta-squared values above 0.14 and subskill effects around 0.21-0.32. Because the reported impacts are medium-to-large in a school-aged sample, the study fits the blue impact tier despite methodological caveats.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT-enhanced Grade 12 quantum theory instruction in which students used a conversational chatbot to ask questions, receive explanations, and support problem solving during course activities compared with traditional teaching.

finding.finding_summary: In a quasi-experimental comparison of ChatGPT-enhanced instruction versus traditional teaching, the experimental group (n=55) outperformed the control group (n=57) on a Quantum Theory achievement test after starting from broadly similar pre-test levels. Post-test means favored the ChatGPT group across Knowing, Applying, and Reasoning (experimental: 15.55, 25.49, 17.51; control: 10.63, 16.89/16.39 as inconsistently reported, 11.73), with reported large effects using eta squared above 0.14 and subskill partial eta squared values of 0.273, 0.206, and 0.263.
finding.measure: Researcher-developed Quantum Theory Test with subscales for Knowing, Applying, and Reasoning; post-test achievement scores
finding.std_deviation: Post-test SDs experimental/control — Knowing: 2.55/1.79, Applying: 3.77/2.86, Reasoning: 3.71/2.99, Overall: 5.89/5.66

finding.finding_summary: Qualitative interviews with students in the ChatGPT condition suggested higher engagement, stronger perceived relevance, and more positive learning experiences than traditional lectures. Students described the chatbot as interactive, accessible, and motivating, though these findings were not supported by validated scales or effect sizes.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview themes on engagement, perceived relevance, and learning experience

finding.finding_summary: Interview data indicated that students perceived improvements in problem-solving, collaboration, and critical-thinking-related processes when using ChatGPT for quantum theory tasks. Students reported using the chatbot to explore multiple solution paths and support group discussion, but these were self-reported perceptions rather than objectively measured durable skills outcomes.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview themes on problem solving, collaboration, and critical thinking
